settings.heading:
The most affordable
Miata EFI.
settings.text: $399. A rusEFI engine computer that plugs into the stock harness, fits the stock case and runs its own wideband. No other plug-in Miata ECU with a built-in wideband costs less.

Stock case & plug

settings.title: The brain
settings.text: One daughterboard runs the engine on every year: an STM32F407 running rusEFI, 8 low-side drivers, 7 protected relay and lamp outputs, 4 ignition outputs and a built-in LSU 4.9 wideband controller.

settings.title: The adapter
settings.text: A motherboard for your model year fits the stock ECU case and takes the stock harness plug. It carries the MAP sensor, the wideband and air-temperature connectors and USB-C.

settings.title: Same brain, every year
settings.text: Every model year gets the same daughterboard, so a fix or a feature lands on all of them.

settings.heading:
Two boards.
One brain.
settings.text: Every unit is two boards stacked on sockets and standoffs.

settings.title: Plug in
settings.text: Fits the stock ECU case and the stock harness plug. Add a wideband sensor and a vacuum hose.

settings.title: Wideband built in
settings.text: An on-board LSU 4.9 controller, the open-source rusEFI design. No separate controller or gauge box.

settings.title: Boost ready
settings.text: A 700 kPa absolute MAP sensor on the board reads vacuum through high boost.

settings.title: Tune over USB-C
settings.text: rusEFI firmware, tuned in TunerStudio. Firmware updates over the same cable.

settings.title: Protected outputs
settings.text: Drivers with current limiting and thermal shutdown, and a separately protected sensor supply.

settings.title: Open
settings.text: rusEFI firmware is open source; the board designs are MIT-licensed.

settings.heading: Find your year
settings.text: One motherboard per model year. The brain is the same on all of them.

settings.question: Which cars does it fit?
settings.answer: The 1989–2005 Mazda MX-5 Miata, NA and NB, with one motherboard per model-year range (see Find your year). Cars swapped from automatic to manual are covered.

settings.question: What else do I need?
settings.answer: A Bosch LSU 4.9 wideband sensor with a bung in the exhaust, a vacuum hose from the board's MAP sensor to the intake manifold, and your car's stock ECU case.

settings.question: Do I need a laptop?
settings.answer: To tune, yes. TunerStudio talks to rusEFI over USB-C, and the firmware has a base setup for each year.

settings.question: Is it street legal?
settings.answer: No. It replaces an emissions-certified engine computer, so it is sold for off-road and competition use only.

settings.question: Is it open source?
settings.answer: The firmware is rusEFI, which is open source. The board designs are MIT-licensed.

settings.question: When does it ship?
settings.answer: The first boards are being built and tested. Sign up below and we'll email you once when the first batch is ready.

settings.heading: Get on the list.
settings.text: One email when it ships. Nothing else.
